headline: High risk: Roo Code’s broad filesystem/network/MCP defaults can conflict with Botpress’s unverified support-bot outputs, creating leakage and cascading-action pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented isolation or provenance controls, so its outputs could be treated as instructions if bridged into Roo Code via files or MCP. Roo Code explicitly supports MCP and workspace-file access, making an injection pathway plausible. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly documented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF Botpress output is copied into a workspace file or MCP message consumed by Roo Code, THEN prompt injection is possible.
IF Roo Code parses Botpress text as instructions without provenance checks, THEN attacker-controlled content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Botpress transcripts into Roo Code.
Require provenance tags on any Botpress-generated text before Roo Code reads it.
Route Botpress output through a human review step before tool execution.
Restrict Roo Code MCP servers to trusted, read-only endpoints.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code reads and writes VS Code workspace files and can call configured model APIs and MCP servers; Botpress is open-source but its data surfaces are not specified here. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could expose source code or screenshots from Roo Code to Botpress flows, or vice versa, so leakage is plausible in default developer setups. The exact pairwise data path is undocumented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Botpress receives workspace files or screenshots exported from Roo Code, THEN source code or visual data may leak.
IF Roo Code forwards Botpress content into a configured third-party model API or MCP server, THEN Botpress data may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep Botpress and Roo Code on separate workspaces.
Do not paste secrets or screenshots from Roo Code into Botpress.
Disable unnecessary MCP servers in Roo Code.
Review outbound API destinations before enabling Roo Code.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has broad write, shell, git, and network capabilities with filesystem-based shared state across instances. Botpress can install packages and is an agentic system, so if both touch the same workspace or repo, concurrent writes and git-state races are credible. Because Roo Code’s defaults are explicitly non-isolated, the conflict can cause destructive or inconsistent state; uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace, THEN file and git-state conflicts can occur.
IF Botpress installs packages while Roo Code edits the same project, THEN dependency and lockfile races are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate repositories or workspace roots.
Pause one agent before the other writes to the repo.
Use git branches per agent.
Avoid concurrent package installation.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared filesystem and git operations.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress can generate support content, and Roo Code can act on workspace files, shell, and MCP tools. If Roo Code treats Botpress output as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or external actions. There is no direct evidence of verification between them, so the pathway is inferred; medium fits because downstream actions are available but not guaranteed.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses Botpress output as a source of facts or instructions without verification, THEN incorrect actions can propagate.
IF Botpress produces malformed support guidance that Roo Code converts into code or commands, THEN downstream errors can amplify.
mitigations: Require human verification before Roo Code executes Botpress-derived steps.
Mark Botpress output as untrusted in prompts and templates.
Use test-only branches for Botpress-driven changes.
Add validation checks before shell or MCP actions.
requires-engineering: implement source-citation and confidence gating.

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is documented only as open-source customer-support software, while Roo Code handles source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so a compliance breach is not established. The main issue is a potential policy gap if support content and code artifacts are mixed, which is smaller than medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Botpress and then copied into Roo Code workspaces, THEN policy review is required.
IF Roo Code is configured to send workspace content to a non-approved model API, THEN retention/residency controls may be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools.
Review model-provider terms before enabling Roo Code.
Separate support transcripts from code repositories.
Document retention settings for any shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: map data classes to approved processing regions.
